gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Human Genetics / Biomedical Sciences; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Catalog admission requirements do not state whether securing a supervisor is required before admission (holistic and onsite review are conducted).

funding.value: Competitive UTRGV assistantships (0.5 FTE, 20 hrs/wk; minimum $1,250/month or $15,000/year for GTA/GRA, $2,400/month or $28,800/year for doctoral Associate Instructors, eligible for non-resident tuition waiver), College of Sciences Dean's Excellence Fellowships ($3,500/year: $2,500 summer stipend + $1,000 travel), and Graduate Select Scholarships (up to $1,000); research is largely funded through STDOI grants.
funding.quote: Get up to $1,000 for your graduate education with the UTRGV Graduate Select Scholarship.

also.quote: Assistantships give students the opportunity to work on campus (up to 20-hour work weeks). | Please visit with your graduate program director about the different assistantships available in your field of study. | careers.utrgv.edu for available graduate assistantship positions. | Eligible for Non-Resident Tuition Waiver: Yes | 10047 – Graduate Teaching Assistant $1,250 $15,000 $11,250 $3,750 | 10095 – Graduate Research Assistant $1,250 $15,000 $11,250 $3,750 | 10064 – Graduate Associate Instructor (doctoral level) $2,400 $28,800 $21,600 $7,200

Fellows selected for this program receive a total of $3,500 per academic year, distributed as follows: Summer Research Support: A $2,500 stipend will be awarded in Summer 2026 and again in Summer 2027 | Conference Travel Funding: Each Fellow will also receive $1,000

A large portion of the Department's research is conducted through the South Texas Diabetes and Obesity Institute (STDOI), a comprehensive interdisciplinary Institute now housed within the UTRGV College of Sciences, which has enjoyed sustained extramural funding for many years.

entry_route.value: Requires a bachelor's degree in an appropriate field from an accredited university and minimum 3.25 GPA (72 credit hours total).
entry_route.quote: degree in an appropriate field of study from an accredited university.

notes: Human Genetics Ph.D. (72 hours, Brownsville/Edinburg STDOI). Requires minimum 3.25 GPA, statement of goals, CV, 3 letters of reference, and holistic plus onsite review. Catalog does not mention GRE.
